domain: Mathematics - analytic number theory and random matrix theory
headline: Do the spacings between zeros of the Riemann zeta function follow the same statistics as the eigenvalues of large random matrices?
landmark: H. L. Montgomery, The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 24 (1973); Montgomery and Dyson's conversation of 1972
tests: a cross-field bridge with no prior in either field's words

domain: Mathematics - finite group theory and modular functions
headline: Are the dimensions of the representations of the largest sporadic simple group related to the coefficients of a classical modular function?
landmark: J. H. Conway and S. P. Norton, Monstrous Moonshine, Bull. London Math. Soc. 11 (1979) 308-339, after McKay's observation of late 1978
tests: a unification question that sounds implausible on its face

headline: Can a single atomic layer of graphite exist as a stable crystal on its own, and do its electrons behave as massless relativistic particles?
landmark: K. S. Novoselov et al., Electric field effect in atomically thin carbon films, Science 306 (2004) 666-669
tests: rule 4: a presupposition contested by the Peierls-Landau argument that 2D crystals are unstable; band structure known since Wallace 1947

headline: Can a material with a negative refractive index be built, and could it focus light more finely than the diffraction limit allows?
landmark: J. B. Pendry, Negative refraction makes a perfect lens, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85 (2000) 3966; D. R. Smith et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 84 (2000) 4184
tests: rule 5: raised by V. G. Veselago (Sov. Phys. Usp. 10, 1968, 509) and little pursued for three decades - an Under-asked case

domain: Computer science - cryptography and complexity theory
headline: Can one convince another party that a statement is true while revealing nothing except the fact that it is true?
landmark: S. Goldwasser, S. Micali and C. Rackoff, The knowledge complexity of interactive proof-systems, STOC 1985 (drafts from 1982-83)
tests: a question that opens a field, with no measurable object

domain: Computer science - AI architecture and learning dynamics
headline: Does a neural network's error fall as a predictable power law in the amount of data and the size of the model, across very different tasks?
landmark: J. Hestness et al., Deep learning scaling is predictable, empirically, arXiv:1712.00409 (2017)
tests: rule 6: learning-curve theory (statistical mechanics of learning, early 1990s) and Banko and Brill (2001) are the same question on other objects

domain: Biology - microbial genome biology and host-virus interaction
headline: Do the clustered regularly interspaced repeats found in many bacterial and archaeal genomes defend the cell against foreign DNA such as viruses?
landmark: F. J. M. Mojica et al., J. Mol. Evol. 60 (2005) 174-182; C. Pourcel et al., Microbiology 151 (2005) 653-663; A. Bolotin et al., Microbiology 151 (2005) 2551-2561; shown by R. Barrangou et al., Science 315 (2007) 1709
tests: a function question where rival functions (DNA repair, replicon partitioning) had been proposed

headline: Can a handful of transcription factors reprogram a fully differentiated adult cell back into an embryonic-like pluripotent cell?
landmark: K. Takahashi and S. Yamanaka, Cell 126 (2006) 663-676
tests: rule 6: MyoD conversion of fibroblasts (Davis, Weintraub and Lassar, Cell 51, 1987) and nuclear transfer and cell fusion are the same idea on other objects

domain: Medicine - gastroenterology and infectious cause of chronic disease
headline: Are chronic gastritis and peptic ulcer disease caused by a bacterial infection of the stomach?
landmark: J. R. Warren; B. Marshall, Lancet 1983;1:1273-1275; B. J. Marshall and J. R. Warren, Lancet 1984;1:1311-1315
tests: rule 4: contested presupposition (the stomach was held to be sterile); spiral organisms in gastric mucosa reported since the 1890s - possibly Under-asked

headline: Can blocking an inhibitory receptor on T cells release an immune response strong enough to reject established tumours?
landmark: D. R. Leach, M. F. Krummel and J. P. Allison, Enhancement of antitumor immunity by CTLA-4 blockade, Science 271 (1996) 1734-1736
tests: a cancer-cure question resting on a then-new finding that CTLA-4 is a negative regulator
